   372	fn dispatch_params(cmdline: &str) -> InitprocArgs {
   373	    let mut result: InitprocArgs = InitprocArgs {
   374	        argv: Vec::new(),
   375	        envp: Vec::new(),
   376	    };
   377	
   378	    let mut kcmdline_end = false;
   379	
   380	    // Step 1: Tokenize and group by normalized parameter name.
   381	    let mut grouped: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(&str, Option<&str>)>> = BTreeMap::new();
   382	
   383	    for arg in split_arg(cmdline) {
   384	        // Everything after "--" goes to init.
   385	        if kcmdline_end {
   386	            result.argv.push(CString::new(arg).unwrap());
   387	            continue;
   388	        }
   389	        if arg == "--" {
   390	            kcmdline_end = true;
   391	            continue;
   392	        }
   393	
   394	        let (key, value) = match arg.find('=') {
   395	            Some(pos) => (&arg[..pos], Some(&arg[pos + 1..])),
   396	            None => (arg, None),
   397	        };
   398	        // Normalize hyphens to underscores (Linux compatibility)
   399	        let normalized = key.replace('-', "_");
   400	        // Group by normalized name, but keep the original key and value for forwarding.
   401	        grouped.entry(normalized).or_default().push((key, value));
   402	    }
   403	
   404	    // Step 2: Build lookup from registered param name to handler.
   405	    let registry: BTreeMap<&str, &KernelParam> = inventory::iter::<KernelParam>
   406	        .into_iter()
   407	        .map(|p| (p.name, p))
   408	        .collect();
   409	
   410	    // Step 3: Dispatch each group to its handler.
   411	    let mut recognized = Vec::new();
   412	    for (name, occurrences) in &grouped {
   413	        if let Some(param) = registry.get(name.as_str()) {
   414	            recognized.push((*param, occurrences));
   415	        } else {
   416	            // Unknown parameter: forward to init
   417	            if name.contains('.') {
   418	                // The entry contains a dot, which is treated as a module argument.
   419	                // Unrecognized module arguments are ignored.
   420	                continue;
   421	            } else if let Some((key, Some(value))) = occurrences.last().copied() {
   422	                // If the entry is not recognized, it is passed to the init process.
   423	                // Pattern 'entry=value' is treated as the init environment.
   424	                let envp_entry = CString::new(key.to_string() + "=" + value).unwrap();
   425	                result.envp.push(envp_entry);
   426	            } else if let Some((key, None)) = occurrences.last().copied() {
   427	                // If the entry is not recognized, it is passed to the init process.
   428	                // Pattern 'entry' without value is treated as the init argument.
   429	                let argv_entry = CString::new(key.to_string()).unwrap();
   430	                result.argv.push(argv_entry);
   431	            } else {
   432	                // This case should not happen since `occurrences` should never be empty.
   433	                debug_assert!(!occurrences.is_empty());
   434	            }
   435	        }
   436	    }
   437	
   438	    // Step 4: Call the setup function for each recognized parameter.
   439	    let (early_params, params): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) =
   440	        recognized.into_iter().partition(|(p, _)| p.early);
   441	    early_params
   442	        .into_iter()
   443	        .chain(params)
   444	        .for_each(|(param, occurrences)| (param.setup)(occurrences));
   445

   153	fn segment_contains(s: &CpuListSegment, cpu: u32) -> bool {
   154	    if cpu < s.start || cpu > s.end {
   155	        return false;
   156	    }
   157	    if s.stride == 0 {

   159	    }
   160

   191	fn parse_cpu_segment(s: &str) -> Result<CpuListSegment, ParamError> {
   192	    // Grammar (pragmatic):
   193	    //   <range> [":" <stride> ["/" <group>] ]
   194	    // where <range> := <n> | <n> "-" <m>
   195	    let (range_part, tail) = match s.split_once(':') {
   196	        Some((a, b)) => (a, Some(b)),
   197	        None => (s, None),
   198	    };
   199	
   200	    let (start, end) = if let Some((a, b)) = range_part.split_once('-') {
   201	        (parse_u32(a)?, parse_u32(b)?)
   202	    } else {
   203	        let n = parse_u32(range_part)?;
   204	        (n, n)
   205	    };
   206	
   207	    if start > end {
   208	        return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   209	    }
   210	
   211	    let (stride, group) = match tail {
   212	        None => (1u32, None),
   213	        Some(t) => {
   214	            if t.is_empty() {
   215	                return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   216	            }
   217	            if let Some((stride_s, group_s)) = t.split_once('/') {
   218	                let stride = parse_u32(stride_s)?;
   219	                let group = parse_u32(group_s)?;
   220	                (stride, Some(group))
   221	            } else {
   222	                (parse_u32(t)?, None)
   223	            }
   224	        }
   225	    };
   226	
   227	    if stride == 0 {
   228	        return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   229	    }
   230	
   231	    if let Some(g) = group
   232	        && g == 0
   233	    {
   234	        return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   235	    }

codex
The command builder confirms two conventions coexist: OSDK puts an `init=...` kernel parameter before `--`, while the NixOS image passes a shell command after `--` and puts the stage-2 `init=...` in init args. I’m separating those so any finding is tied to an actual changed path, not a different boot mode.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0

use clap::ValueEnum;

use std::path::PathBuf;

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BootScheme {
    /// Command line arguments for the guest kernel
    #[serde(default)]
    pub kcmd_args: Vec<String>,
    /// Command line arguments for the guest init process
    #[serde(default)]
    pub init_args: Vec<String>,
    /// The path of initramfs
    pub initramfs: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// The infrastructures used to boot the guest
    pub method: Option<BootMethod>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, ValueEnum)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum BootMethod {
    /// Boot the kernel by making a rescue CD image.
    GrubRescueIso,
    /// Boot the kernel by making a Qcow2 image with Grub as the bootloader.
    GrubQcow2,
    /// Use the [QEMU direct boot](https://qemu-project.gitlab.io/qemu/system/linuxboot.html)
    /// to boot the kernel with QEMU's built-in Seabios and Coreboot utilities.
    #[default]
    QemuDirect,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Boot {
    pub kcmdline: Vec<String>,
    pub initramfs: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub method: BootMethod,
}

impl BootScheme {
    pub fn inherit(&mut self, from: &Self) {
        self.kcmd_args = {
            let mut kcmd_args = from.kcmd_args.clone();
            kcmd_args.extend(self.kcmd_args.clone());
            kcmd_args
        };
        self.init_args = {
            let mut init_args = from.init_args.clone();
            init_args.extend(self.init_args.clone());
            init_args
        };
        if self.initramfs.is_none() {
            self.initramfs.clone_from(&from.initramfs);
        }
        if self.method.is_none() {
            self.method = from.method;
        }
    }

    pub fn finalize(self) -> Boot {
        let mut kcmdline = self.kcmd_args;
        kcmdline.push("--".to_owned());
        kcmdline.extend(self.init_args);
        Boot {
            kcmdline,
            initramfs: self.initramfs,
            method: self.method.unwrap_or(BootMethod::QemuDirect),
        }
    }
}

    62	    /// Expand to concrete CPU IDs, returning at most `max_elems` elements.
    63	    ///
    64	    /// Note: if the CPU list expands to more than `max_elems`, the result is truncated.
    65	    pub fn expand_bounded(&self, max_elems: usize) -> Result<Vec<u32>, ParamError> {
    66	        if max_elems == 0 {
    67	            return Ok(Vec::new());
    68	        }
    69	
    70	        let mut out = Vec::new();
    71	
    72	        // Helper: push a cpu id; if we reached the bound, stop expansion.
    73	        let push_or_done = |out: &mut Vec<u32>, cpu: u32| -> bool {
    74	            if out.len() >= max_elems {
    75	                return true;
    76	            }
    77	            out.push(cpu);
    78	            out.len() >= max_elems
    79	        };
    80

    14	/// Prints the formatted arguments to the standard output.
    15	pub fn _print(args: fmt::Arguments) {
    16	    // We must call `all_devices_lock` instead of `all_devices` here, as `all_devices` invokes the
    17	    // `clone` method of `String` and `Arc`, which may lead to a deadlock when there is low memory
    18	    // in the heap. (The heap allocator will log a message when memory is low.)
    19	    //
    20	    // Also, holding the lock will prevent the logs from interleaving.
    21	    let devices = aster_console::all_devices_lock();
    22	
    23	    struct Printer<'a>(
    24	        SpinLockGuard<'a, BTreeMap<String, Arc<dyn AnyConsoleDevice>>, LocalIrqDisabled>,
    25	    );
    26	    impl Write for Printer<'_> {
    27	        fn write_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> fmt::Result {
    28	            if self.0.is_empty() {
    29	                ostd::early_print!("{}", s);
    30	            } else {
    31	                for console in self.0.values() {
    32	                    console.send(s.as_bytes());
    33	                }
    34	            }
    35	            Ok(())
    36	        }
    37	    }
    38	
    39	    Printer(devices).write_fmt(args).unwrap();
    40	}
    41

    44	macro_rules! print {
    45	    ($($arg:tt)*) => {{

   121	/// An I8042 PS/2 Controller.
   122	pub(super) struct I8042Controller {
   123	    data_port: IoPort<u8, ReadWriteAccess>,
   124	    status_or_command_port: IoPort<u8, ReadWriteAccess>,
   125	}
   126	
   127	impl I8042Controller {
   128	    fn new() -> Result<Self, I8042ControllerError> {
   129	        const DATA_PORT_ADDR: u16 = 0x60;
   130	        const STATUS_OR_COMMAND_PORT_ADDR: u16 = 0x64;
   131	
   132	        if !Self::is_present_acpi() {
   133	            // The PS/2 controller does not exist. See:
   134	            // <https://uefi.org/specs/ACPI/6.5/05_ACPI_Software_Programming_Model.html#ia-pc-boot-architecture-flags>.
   135	            //
   136	            // However, it may actually be present and enumerable from other sources, such as PnP
   137	            // devices. See:
   138	            // <https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.18/source/drivers/input/serio/i8042-acpipnpio.h#L1578>.
   139	            //
   140	            // Currently, we lack the necessary support, so we allow the user to manually override
   141	            // the ACPI flag by appending "i8042.exist" to the kernel command line.
   142	            //
   143	            // TODO: Add support for enumerating PnP devices and remove the command line option.
   144	            if !Self::is_present_cmdline() {
   145	                log::info!(
   146	                    "ACPI says i8042 controller is absent; \
   147	                    if it is incorrect, append 'i8042.exist' in cmdline to override it"
   148	                );
   149	                return Err(I8042ControllerError::NotPresent);
   150	            } else {
   151	                log::info!(
   152	                    "ACPI says i8042 controller is absent; \
   153	                    however, it is overridden by 'i8042.exist' in cmdline"
   154	                );
   155	            }
   156	        } else {
   157	            log::info!("ACPI says i8042 controller is present");
   158	        }
   159	
   160	        let controller = Self {
   161	            data_port: IoPort::acquire(DATA_PORT_ADDR).unwrap(),
   162	            status_or_command_port: IoPort::acquire(STATUS_OR_COMMAND_PORT_ADDR).unwrap(),
   163	        };
   164	        Ok(controller)
   165	    }
   166	
   167	    fn is_present_acpi() -> bool {
   168	        ACPI_INFO
   169	            .get()
   170	            .unwrap()
   171	            .boot_flags
   172	            .is_some_and(|flags| flags.motherboard_implements_8042())
   173	    }
   174	
   175	    /// Checks if the kernel command line contains the "i8042.exist" option.
   176	    fn is_present_cmdline() -> bool {
   177	        I8042_EXIST.get().copied().unwrap_or(false)
   178	    }

   245	fn parse_u32(s: &str) -> Result<u32, ParamError> {
   246	    if s.is_empty() {

   248	    }
   249	    s.parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParamError::InvalidValue)
   250	}
   251	
   252	impl ParseParamValue for MetricU64 {
   253	    fn parse_param(value: &str) -> Result<Self, ParamError> {
   254	        if value.is_empty() {
   255	            return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   256	        }
   257	
   258	        let (num_part, suf) = match value.chars().last() {
   259	            Some(c) if c.is_ascii_alphabetic() => (&value[..value.len() - c.len_utf8()], Some(c)),
   260	            _ => (value, None),
   261	        };
   262	
   263	        if num_part.is_empty() {
   264	            return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   265	        }
   266	
   267	        let base: u64 = num_part.parse().map_err(|_| ParamError::InvalidValue)?;
   268	        let mul: u64 = match suf.map(|c| c.to_ascii_uppercase()) {
   269	            None => 1,
   270	            Some('K') => 1024u64,
   271	            Some('M') => 1024u64.pow(2),
   272	            Some('G') => 1024u64.pow(3),
   273	            Some('T') => 1024u64.pow(4),
   274	            Some('P') => 1024u64.pow(5),
   275	            _ => return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue),
   276	        };
   277	
   278	        base.checked_mul(mul)
   279	            .map(MetricU64)
   280	            .ok_or(ParamError::InvalidValue)
   281	    }
   282	}

## Correctness

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/lib.rs` line 412

> ```diff
> 380     // Step 1: Tokenize and group by normalized parameter name.
> 381     let mut grouped: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(&str, Option<&str>)>> = BTreeMap::new();
> ...
> 412     for (name, occurrences) in &grouped {
> ...
> 421             } else if let Some((key, Some(value))) = occurrences.last().copied() {
> ...
> 426             } else if let Some((key, None)) = occurrences.last().copied() {
> ```

Incorrect argument forwarding (major): `dispatch_params()` stores pre-`--` arguments in a `BTreeMap` and later forwards unknown entries by iterating that map, so init arguments are sorted by key and duplicate bare arguments are collapsed with `occurrences.last()`. A command line such as `init=/usr/bin/busybox zarg aarg zarg` should pass `zarg`, `aarg`, `zarg` to `init` in that order, but this loop forwards only `aarg`, `zarg`.

**Fix.** Preserve forwarding order while still grouping recognized parameters. One practical shape is to build `registry` first, parse tokens in command-line order, push unknown `argv`/`envp` entries immediately, and only group occurrences for keys found in `registry`.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/types.rs` line 166

> ```diff
> 110             // Grouped selection:
> 111             // for each group window [start+gb, start+gb+g), emit start+gb+within for within=0,stride,2*stride...
> ...
> 161     let offset = cpu - s.start;
> 162     if let Some(g) = s.group {
> ...
> 166         let in_group_offset = offset % g;
> 167         in_group_offset.is_multiple_of(s.stride)
> ```

Wrong CPU list parsing (major): `CpuList` treats the `:2/4` Linux CPU-list form as a stride of `2` inside each group of `4`, but Linux-style grouped CPU lists use the first number as the used-size of each group. For `CpuList::parse_param("0-9:2/4")`, `contains(1)` returns `false` and `contains(2)` returns `true`; the expected selected CPUs are `0`, `1`, `4`, `5`, `8`, and `9`.

**Fix.** Model the grouped form as `used_size/group_size` instead of `stride/group`. `contains()` should check `in_group_offset < used_size`, and `expand_bounded()` should emit the first `used_size` CPUs from each `group_size` window, clipping at `end`.

### `kernel/comps/i8042/src/controller.rs` line 177

> ```diff
> 132         if !Self::is_present_acpi() {
> ...
> 175     /// Checks if the kernel command line contains the "i8042.exist" option.
> 176     fn is_present_cmdline() -> bool {
> 177         I8042_EXIST.get().copied().unwrap_or(false)
> 178     }
> ```

Incorrect override handling (major): `is_present_cmdline()` collapses an absent command-line override and an explicit `i8042.exist=0` into the same `false` value, and `I8042Controller::new()` only consults it when ACPI says the controller is absent. On a machine where ACPI reports i8042 present, `i8042.exist=0` is parsed but ignored, so the driver still probes instead of honoring the skip request.

**Fix.** Keep the override tri-state, for example return `Option<bool>` from the command-line helper and match it before falling back to ACPI: `Some(false)` should return `I8042ControllerError::NotPresent`, `Some(true)` should force probing, and `None` should use `is_present_acpi()`.

### `kernel/comps/logger/src/console.rs` line 29

> ```diff
> 21     let devices = aster_console::all_devices_lock();
> ...
> 27         fn write_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> fmt::Result {
> 28             if self.0.is_empty() {
> 29                 ostd::early_print!("{}", s);
> 30             } else {
> ```

`no-io-under-spinlock` (major): `_print()` holds the `all_devices_lock()` `SpinLockGuard` when `write_str()` calls `ostd::early_print!`. With no registered consoles, every log write does serial output while local IRQs are disabled and the console-device spinlock is held, so a slow or blocking serial path can stall code that needs IRQ progress or the same lock.

**Fix.** Handle the empty-console case before constructing `Printer`, then drop `devices` before calling `ostd::early_print!`. For example, check `devices.is_empty()`, call `drop(devices)`, print with `ostd::early_print!("{}", args)`, and return.

    62	    /// Expand to concrete CPU IDs, returning at most `max_elems` elements.
    63	    ///
    64	    /// Note: if the CPU list expands to more than `max_elems`, the result is truncated.
    65	    pub fn expand_bounded(&self, max_elems: usize) -> Result<Vec<u32>, ParamError> {
    66	        if max_elems == 0 {
    67	            return Ok(Vec::new());
    68	        }
    69	
    70	        let mut out = Vec::new();
    71	
    72	        // Helper: push a cpu id; if we reached the bound, stop expansion.
    73	        let push_or_done = |out: &mut Vec<u32>, cpu: u32| -> bool {
    74	            if out.len() >= max_elems {
    75	                return true;
    76	            }
    77	            out.push(cpu);
    78	            out.len() >= max_elems
    79	        };
    80	
    81	        for s in &self.segments {
    82	            if s.stride == 0 {
    83	                return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
    84	            }
    85	            if let Some(g) = s.group
    86	                && g == 0
    87	            {
    88	                return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
    89	            }
    90	            if s.start > s.end {
    91	                return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
    92	            }
    93	
    94	            // Fast path: no group => arithmetic progression from start to end by stride.
    95	            if s.group.is_none() {
    96	                let mut cur = s.start;
    97	                while cur <= s.end {
    98	                    if push_or_done(&mut out, cur) {
    99	                        return Ok(out);
   100	                    }
   101	
   102	                    match cur.checked_add(s.stride) {
   103	                        Some(n) => cur = n,
   104	                        None => break,
   105	                    }
   106	                }
   107	                continue;
   108	            }
   109	
   110	            // Grouped selection:
   111	            // for each group window [start+gb, start+gb+g), emit start+gb+within for within=0,stride,2*stride...
   112	            let g = s.group.unwrap();
   113	            let stride = s.stride;
   114	
   115	            let mut gb: u32 = 0;
   116	            while let Some(v) = s.start.checked_add(gb) {
   117	                let group_start = v;
   118	                if group_start > s.end {
   119	                    break;
   120	                }
   121	
   122	                let mut within: u32 = 0;
   123	                while within < g {
   124	                    let cpu = match group_start.checked_add(within) {
   125	                        Some(v) => v,
   126	                        None => break,
   127	                    };
   128	                    if cpu > s.end {
   129	                        break;
   130	                    }
   131	
   132	                    if push_or_done(&mut out, cpu) {
   133	                        return Ok(out);
   134	                    }
   135	
   136	                    match within.checked_add(stride) {
   137	                        Some(n) => within = n,
   138	                        None => break,
   139	                    }
   140	                }
   141	
   142	                match gb.checked_add(g) {
   143	                    Some(n) => gb = n,
   144	                    None => break,
   145	                }
   146	            }
   147	        }
   148	
   149	        Ok(out)
   150	    }
   151	}

   153	fn segment_contains(s: &CpuListSegment, cpu: u32) -> bool {
   154	    if cpu < s.start || cpu > s.end {
   155	        return false;
   156	    }
   157	    if s.stride == 0 {
   158	        return false;
   159	    }
   160	
   161	    let offset = cpu - s.start;
   162	    if let Some(g) = s.group {
   163	        if g == 0 {
   164	            return false;
   165	        }
   166	        let in_group_offset = offset % g;
   167	        in_group_offset.is_multiple_of(s.stride)
   168	    } else {
   169	        offset.is_multiple_of(s.stride)
   170	    }
   171	}

   173	impl ParseParamValue for CpuList {
   174	    fn parse_param(value: &str) -> Result<Self, ParamError> {
   175	        if value.is_empty() {
   176	            return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   177	        }
   178	
   179	        let mut segments = Vec::new();
   180	        for part in value.split(',') {
   181	            if part.is_empty() {
   182	                return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   183	            }
   184	            segments.push(parse_cpu_segment(part)?);
   185	        }
   186	
   187	        Ok(CpuList { segments })
   188	    }
   189	}
   190	
   191	fn parse_cpu_segment(s: &str) -> Result<CpuListSegment, ParamError> {
   192	    // Grammar (pragmatic):
   193	    //   <range> [":" <stride> ["/" <group>] ]
   194	    // where <range> := <n> | <n> "-" <m>
   195	    let (range_part, tail) = match s.split_once(':') {
   196	        Some((a, b)) => (a, Some(b)),
   197	        None => (s, None),
   198	    };
   199	
   200	    let (start, end) = if let Some((a, b)) = range_part.split_once('-') {
   201	        (parse_u32(a)?, parse_u32(b)?)
   202	    } else {
   203	        let n = parse_u32(range_part)?;
   204	        (n, n)
   205	    };
   206	
   207	    if start > end {
   208	        return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   209	    }
   210	
   211	    let (stride, group) = match tail {
   212	        None => (1u32, None),
   213	        Some(t) => {
   214	            if t.is_empty() {
   215	                return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   216	            }
   217	            if let Some((stride_s, group_s)) = t.split_once('/') {
   218	                let stride = parse_u32(stride_s)?;
   219	                let group = parse_u32(group_s)?;
   220	                (stride, Some(group))
   221	            } else {
   222	                (parse_u32(t)?, None)
   223	            }
   224	        }
   225	    };
   226	
   227	    if stride == 0 {
   228	        return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   229	    }
   230	
   231	    if let Some(g) = group
   232	        && g == 0
   233	    {
   234	        return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   235	    }
   236	
   237	    Ok(CpuListSegment {
   238	        start,
   239	        end,
   240	        stride,
   241	        group,
   242	    })
   243	}
   244	
   245	fn parse_u32(s: &str) -> Result<u32, ParamError> {
   246	    if s.is_empty() {
   247	        return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   248	    }
   249	    s.parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParamError::InvalidValue)
   250	}

   252	impl ParseParamValue for MetricU64 {
   253	    fn parse_param(value: &str) -> Result<Self, ParamError> {
   254	        if value.is_empty() {
   255	            return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   256	        }
   257	
   258	        let (num_part, suf) = match value.chars().last() {
   259	            Some(c) if c.is_ascii_alphabetic() => (&value[..value.len() - c.len_utf8()], Some(c)),
   260	            _ => (value, None),
   261	        };
   262	
   263	        if num_part.is_empty() {
   264	            return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue);
   265	        }
   266	
   267	        let base: u64 = num_part.parse().map_err(|_| ParamError::InvalidValue)?;
   268	        let mul: u64 = match suf.map(|c| c.to_ascii_uppercase()) {
   269	            None => 1,
   270	            Some('K') => 1024u64,
   271	            Some('M') => 1024u64.pow(2),
   272	            Some('G') => 1024u64.pow(3),
   273	            Some('T') => 1024u64.pow(4),
   274	            Some('P') => 1024u64.pow(5),
   275	            _ => return Err(ParamError::InvalidValue),
   276	        };
   277	
   278	        base.checked_mul(mul)
   279	            .map(MetricU64)
   280	            .ok_or(ParamError::InvalidValue)
   281	    }
   282	}

   254	impl<T: FromStr> ParseParamValue for T {
   255	    fn parse_param(value: &str) -> Result<Self, ParamError> {
   256	        value.parse().map_err(|_| ParamError::InvalidValue)
   257	    }
   258	}

   260	/// A `Vec<T>` where `T: FromStr` can be a repeatable parameter.
   261	/// (No coherence conflict: `Vec<T>` does not implement `FromStr`.)
   262	impl<T: FromStr> ParseRepeatableParamValue for Vec<T> {
   263	    fn parse_all(values: &[&str]) -> Result<Self, ParamError> {
   264	        values
   265	            .iter()
   266	            .map(|v| v.parse().map_err(|_| ParamError::InvalidValue))
   267	            .collect()
   268	    }
   269	}

   271	/// `bool` as a flag: bare flag means `true`; "flag=1"/"flag=on" also accepted.
   272	impl ParseFlag for bool {
   273	    fn parse_flag(value: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self, ParamError> {
   274	        match value {
   275	            None | Some("1") | Some("on") | Some("yes") | Some("true") => Ok(true),
   276	            Some("0") | Some("off") | Some("no") | Some("false") => Ok(false),
   277	            _ => Err(ParamError::InvalidValue),
   278	        }
   279	    }
   280	}

   291	/// Helper for single-value key-value parameters (last-wins).
   292	pub fn setup_kv_param<S: ParamStorage>(
   293	    storage: &S,
   294	    occurrences: &[(&str, Option<&str>)],
   295	    name: &str,
   296	) where
   297	    S::Value: ParseParamValue,
   298	{
   299	    let last = match occurrences.last() {
   300	        Some((_, val)) => *val, // Option<&str> is Copy
   301	        None => return,
   302	    };
   303	    match last {
   304	        Some(value) => match S::Value::parse_param(value) {
   305	            Ok(v) => storage.store_param(v),
   306	            Err(_) => log::warn!("invalid value for kernel parameter '{}'", name),
   307	        },
   308	        None => log::warn!("kernel parameter '{}' requires a value", name),
   309	    }
   310	}
   311	
   312	/// Helper for repeatable key-value parameters (all occurrences).
   313	pub fn setup_repeatable_kv_param<S: ParamStorage>(
   314	    storage: &S,
   315	    occurrences: &[(&str, Option<&str>)],
   316	    name: &str,
   317	) where
   318	    S::Value: ParseRepeatableParamValue,
   319	{
   320	    let values: Vec<&str> = occurrences.iter().filter_map(|(_, val)| *val).collect();
   321	    if values.is_empty() {
   322	        log::warn!("repeatable parameter '{}' requires values", name);
   323	        return;
   324	    }
   325	    match S::Value::parse_all(&values) {
   326	        Ok(v) => storage.store_param(v),
   327	        Err(_) => log::warn!("invalid value for kernel parameter '{}'", name),
   328	    }
   329	}
   330	
   331	/// Helper for flag parameters (last-wins, optional value).
   332	pub fn setup_flag_param<S: ParamStorage>(
   333	    storage: &S,
   334	    occurrences: &[(&str, Option<&str>)],
   335	    name: &str,
   336	) where
   337	    S::Value: ParseFlag,
   338	{
   339	    let last = match occurrences.last() {
   340	        Some((_, val)) => *val,
   341	        None => return,
   342	    };
   343	    match S::Value::parse_flag(last) {
   344	        Ok(v) => storage.store_param(v),
   345	        Err(_) => log::warn!("invalid value for flag '{}'", name),
   346	    }
   347	}

   358	// Splits the command line string by spaces but preserve
   359	// ones that are protected by double quotes(`"`).
   360	fn split_arg(input: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
   361	    let mut inside_quotes = false;
   362	
   363	    input.split(move |c: char| {
   364	        if c == '"' {
   365	            inside_quotes = !inside_quotes;
   366	        }
   367	
   368	        !inside_quotes && c.is_whitespace()
   369	    })
   370	}
   371	
   372	fn dispatch_params(cmdline: &str) -> InitprocArgs {
   373	    let mut result: InitprocArgs = InitprocArgs {
   374	        argv: Vec::new(),
   375	        envp: Vec::new(),
   376	    };
   377	
   378	    let mut kcmdline_end = false;
   379	
   380	    // Step 1: Tokenize and group by normalized parameter name.
   381	    let mut grouped: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(&str, Option<&str>)>> = BTreeMap::new();
   382	
   383	    for arg in split_arg(cmdline) {
   384	        // Everything after "--" goes to init.
   385	        if kcmdline_end {
   386	            result.argv.push(CString::new(arg).unwrap());
   387	            continue;
   388	        }
   389	        if arg == "--" {
   390	            kcmdline_end = true;
   391	            continue;
   392	        }
   393	
   394	        let (key, value) = match arg.find('=') {
   395	            Some(pos) => (&arg[..pos], Some(&arg[pos + 1..])),
   396	            None => (arg, None),
   397	        };
   398	        // Normalize hyphens to underscores (Linux compatibility)
   399	        let normalized = key.replace('-', "_");
   400	        // Group by normalized name, but keep the original key and value for forwarding.
   401	        grouped.entry(normalized).or_default().push((key, value));
   402	    }
   403	
   404	    // Step 2: Build lookup from registered param name to handler.
   405	    let registry: BTreeMap<&str, &KernelParam> = inventory::iter::<KernelParam>
   406	        .into_iter()
   407	        .map(|p| (p.name, p))
   408	        .collect();
   409	
   410	    // Step 3: Dispatch each group to its handler.
   411	    let mut recognized = Vec::new();
   412	    for (name, occurrences) in &grouped {
   413	        if let Some(param) = registry.get(name.as_str()) {
   414	            recognized.push((*param, occurrences));
   415	        } else {
   416	            // Unknown parameter: forward to init
   417	            if name.contains('.') {
   418	                // The entry contains a dot, which is treated as a module argument.
   419	                // Unrecognized module arguments are ignored.
   420	                continue;
   421	            } else if let Some((key, Some(value))) = occurrences.last().copied() {
   422	                // If the entry is not recognized, it is passed to the init process.
   423	                // Pattern 'entry=value' is treated as the init environment.
   424	                let envp_entry = CString::new(key.to_string() + "=" + value).unwrap();
   425	                result.envp.push(envp_entry);
   426	            } else if let Some((key, None)) = occurrences.last().copied() {
   427	                // If the entry is not recognized, it is passed to the init process.
   428	                // Pattern 'entry' without value is treated as the init argument.
   429	                let argv_entry = CString::new(key.to_string()).unwrap();
   430	                result.argv.push(argv_entry);
   431	            } else {
   432	                // This case should not happen since `occurrences` should never be empty.
   433	                debug_assert!(!occurrences.is_empty());
   434	            }
   435	        }
   436	    }
   437	
   438	    // Step 4: Call the setup function for each recognized parameter.
   439	    let (early_params, params): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) =
   440	        recognized.into_iter().partition(|(p, _)| p.early);
   441	    early_params
   442	        .into_iter()
   443	        .chain(params)
   444	        .for_each(|(param, occurrences)| (param.setup)(occurrences));
   445	
   446	    result
   447	}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0

//! Console output.

use core::fmt::{Arguments, Write};

use crate::arch::serial::SERIAL_PORT;

pub mod uart_ns16650a;

/// Prints formatted arguments to the console.
pub fn early_print(args: Arguments) {
    let Some(serial) = SERIAL_PORT.get() else {
        return;
    };

    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
    crate::arch::if_tdx_enabled!({
        // Hold the lock to prevent the logs from interleaving.
        let _guard = serial.lock();
        tdx_guest::print(args);
    } else {
        serial.lock().write_fmt(args).unwrap();
    });
    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
    serial.lock().write_fmt(args).unwrap();
}

/// Prints to the console.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! early_print {
    ($fmt: literal $(, $($arg: tt)+)?) => {
        $crate::console::early_print(format_args!($fmt $(, $($arg)+)?))
    }
}

/// Prints to the console with a newline.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! early_println {

    78	// Splits the command line string by spaces but preserve
    79	// ones that are protected by double quotes(`"`).
    80	fn split_arg(input: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
    81	    let mut inside_quotes = false;
    82	
    83	    input.split(move |c: char| {
    84	        if c == '"' {
    85	            inside_quotes = !inside_quotes;
    86	        }
    87	
    88	        !inside_quotes && c.is_whitespace()
    89	    })
    90	}
    91	
    92	// Define the way to parse a string to `KCmdlineArg`.
    93	impl From<&str> for KCmdlineArg {
    94	    fn from(cmdline: &str) -> Self {
    95	        // What we construct.
    96	        let mut result: KCmdlineArg = KCmdlineArg {
    97	            initproc: InitprocArgs {
    98	                path: None,
    99	                argv: Vec::new(),
   100	                envp: Vec::new(),
   101	            },
   102	            console_names: Vec::new(),
   103	            module_args: BTreeMap::new(),
   104	        };
   105	
   106	        // Every thing after the "--" mark is the init arguments.
   107	        let mut kcmdline_end = false;
   108	
   109	        // The main parse loop. The processing steps are arranged (not very strictly)
   110	        // by the analysis over the Backus–Naur form syntax tree.
   111	        for arg in split_arg(cmdline) {
   112	            // Cmdline => KernelArg "--" InitArg
   113	            // KernelArg => Arg "\s+" KernelArg | %empty
   114	            // InitArg => Arg "\s+" InitArg | %empty
   115	            if kcmdline_end {
   116	                if result.initproc.path.is_none() {
   117	                    panic!("[KCmdline] Init arguments specified without init process");
   118	                }
   119	                result.initproc.argv.push(CString::new(arg).unwrap());
   120	                continue;
   121	            }
   122	            if arg == "--" {
   123	                kcmdline_end = true;
   124	                continue;
   125	            }
   126	            // Arg => Entry | Entry "=" Value
   127	            let arg_pattern: Vec<_> = arg.split('=').collect();
   128	            let (entry, value) = match arg_pattern.len() {
   129	                1 => (arg_pattern[0], None),
   130	                2 => (arg_pattern[0], Some(arg_pattern[1])),
   131	                _ => {
   132	                    log::warn!(
   133	                        "[KCmdline] Unable to parse kernel argument {}, skip for now",
   134	                        arg
   135	                    );
   136	                    continue;
   137	                }
   138	            };
   139	            // Entry => Module "." ModuleOptionName | KernelOptionName
   140	            let entry_pattern: Vec<_> = entry.split('.').collect();
   141	            let (node, option) = match entry_pattern.len() {
   142	                1 => (None, entry_pattern[0]),
   143	                2 => (Some(entry_pattern[0]), entry_pattern[1]),
   144	                _ => {
   145	                    log::warn!(
   146	                        "[KCmdline] Unable to parse entry {} in argument {}, skip for now",
   147	                        entry,
   148	                        arg
   149	                    );
   150	                    continue;
   151	                }
   152	            };
   153	            if let Some(modname) = node {
   154	                let modarg = if let Some(v) = value {
   155	                    ModuleArg::KeyVal(
   156	                        CString::new(option.to_string()).unwrap(),
   157	                        CString::new(v).unwrap(),
   158	                    )
   159	                } else {
   160	                    ModuleArg::Arg(CString::new(option).unwrap())
   161	                };
   162	                result
   163	                    .module_args
   164	                    .entry(modname.to_string())
   165	                    .and_modify(|v| v.push(modarg.clone()))
   166	                    .or_insert(vec![modarg.clone()]);
   167	                continue;
   168	            }
   169	            // KernelOptionName => /*literal string alternatives*/ | /*init environment*/
   170	            if let Some(value) = value {
   171	                // The option has a value.
   172	                match option {
   173	                    "init" => {
   174	                        if result.initproc.path.is_some() {
   175	                            panic!("[KCmdline] Init process specified twice");
   176	                        }
   177	                        result.initproc.path = Some(value.to_string());
   178	                    }
   179	                    "console" => {
   180	                        result.console_names.push(value.to_string());
   181	                    }
   182	                    _ => {
   183	                        // If the option is not recognized, it is passed to the init process.
   184	                        // Pattern 'option=value' is treated as the init environment.
   185	                        let envp_entry = CString::new(option.to_string() + "=" + value).unwrap();
   186	                        result.initproc.envp.push(envp_entry);
   187	                    }
   188	                }
   189	            } else {
   190	                // There is no value, the entry is only a option.
   191	
   192	                // If the option is not recognized, it is passed to the init process.
   193	                // Pattern 'option' without value is treated as the init argument.
   194	                let argv_entry = CString::new(option.to_string()).unwrap();
   195	                result.initproc.argv.push(argv_entry);
   196	            }
   197	        }
   198	
   199	        result
   200	    }
   201	}
   202

# Summary

The series adds a useful registry-based command-line parameter framework, moves `init`, `console`, and `i8042.exist` onto it, and adds reusable parsers plus boot-test coverage. The main risks are behavioral: unknown init arguments lose ordering and duplicates, Linux grouped CPU-list syntax is parsed incorrectly, and the `i8042.exist=0` path is documented and parsed but not honored when ACPI reports the controller present.

Top issues to fix first:

- Preserve command-line order for unknown parameters forwarded to `init`; the new `BTreeMap` grouping changes observable argv/envp behavior.
- Correct the `CpuList` grouped-range semantics to match Linux's `<used size>/<group size>` syntax.
- Decide the intended `i8042.exist` contract and make implementation and docs agree, preferably with tri-state override handling.
- Avoid serial I/O while holding the console-device spinlock in the early fallback logger.

Structurally, tighten the new public API before it grows users: avoid module-wide lint suppression, keep registry/value internals private behind constructors and getters, and put the new `inventory` dependency under workspace dependency management.

## Maintainability

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/Cargo.toml` line 13

> ```diff
> ```diff

>  log.workspace = true
>  ostd.workspace = true
>  spin.workspace = true

> ```
> ```

`workspace-deps` (minor): `kernel/comps/cmdline/Cargo.toml` adds `inventory` with an inline git specification while this workspace centralizes member dependencies in root `Cargo.toml` and member crates use `.workspace = true`. This creates another version pin to update independently.

**Fix.** Move the `inventory` specification to root `[workspace.dependencies]`, then depend on it here as `inventory.workspace = true`.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/lib.rs` line 179

`information-hiding` (minor): `InitprocArgs::argv` and `InitprocArgs::envp` return `&Vec<CString>`, which exposes the storage choice even though callers only need a borrowed sequence. That makes future representation changes harder and is less idiomatic than returning a slice.

**Fix.** Return slices from both getters: `pub fn argv(&self) -> &[CString]` and `pub fn envp(&self) -> &[CString]`. Existing callers can still use `.to_vec()`.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/lib.rs` line 284

`getter-encapsulation` (major): `KernelParam` exposes `name`, `setup`, and `early` as public fields, even though they are registry internals used by the exported macros. External code can now construct and depend on the raw `KernelParam` representation, so changing registration details later becomes a public API break.

**Fix.** Make `KernelParam` fields private, add public constructor functions used by the macros, and mark any macro-only support surface as `#[doc(hidden)]`.

The workspace uses `#[expect(dead_code)]` for intentional dead code, and the guideline asks suppressions to cover the smallest necessary scope.

**Fix.** Remove the module-level `#![allow(dead_code)]`. Either wire `CpuList` and `MetricU64` into real parameter users now, or mark only the currently unused items with narrow `#[expect(dead_code)]` plus the concrete planned use.

> +    /// Step within range, default 1.
> +    pub stride: u32,
> +    /// Optional group size (the `/N` part). When present, stride selection is
> +    /// applied within each group window.
> +    pub group: Option<u32>,
> +}
> ```
> ```

`rust-type-invariants` (major): `CpuListSegment` has public fields, so callers can construct invalid segments such as `CpuListSegment { start: 4, end: 1, stride: 0, group: Some(0) }`. The parser enforces those invariants, but the type itself does not.

**Fix.** Keep `CpuListSegment` fields private and expose getters, plus a validating constructor if external construction is needed.

## Correctness

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/lib.rs` line 412

> ```diff
> 380     // Step 1: Tokenize and group by normalized parameter name.
> 381     let mut grouped: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(&str, Option<&str>)>> = BTreeMap::new();
> ...
> 412     for (name, occurrences) in &grouped {
> ...
> 421             } else if let Some((key, Some(value))) = occurrences.last().copied() {
> ...
> 426             } else if let Some((key, None)) = occurrences.last().copied() {
> ```

Incorrect argument forwarding (major): `dispatch_params()` stores pre-`--` arguments in a `BTreeMap` and later forwards unknown entries by iterating that map, so init arguments are sorted by key and duplicate bare arguments are collapsed with `occurrences.last()`. A command line such as `init=/usr/bin/busybox zarg aarg zarg` should pass `zarg`, `aarg`, `zarg` to `init` in that order, but this loop forwards only `aarg`, `zarg`.

**Fix.** Preserve forwarding order while still grouping recognized parameters. One practical shape is to build `registry` first, parse tokens in command-line order, push unknown `argv`/`envp` entries immediately, and only group occurrences for keys found in `registry`.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/types.rs` line 166

> ```diff
> 110             // Grouped selection:
> 111             // for each group window [start+gb, start+gb+g), emit start+gb+within for within=0,stride,2*stride...
> ...
> 161     let offset = cpu - s.start;
> 162     if let Some(g) = s.group {
> ...
> 166         let in_group_offset = offset % g;
> 167         in_group_offset.is_multiple_of(s.stride)
> ```

Wrong CPU list parsing (major): `CpuList` treats the `:2/4` Linux CPU-list form as a stride of `2` inside each group of `4`, but Linux-style grouped CPU lists use the first number as the used-size of each group. For `CpuList::parse_param("0-9:2/4")`, `contains(1)` returns `false` and `contains(2)` returns `true`; the expected selected CPUs are `0`, `1`, `4`, `5`, `8`, and `9`.

**Fix.** Model the grouped form as `used_size/group_size` instead of `stride/group`. `contains()` should check `in_group_offset < used_size`, and `expand_bounded()` should emit the first `used_size` CPUs from each `group_size` window, clipping at `end`.

### `kernel/comps/i8042/src/controller.rs` line 177

> ```diff
> 132         if !Self::is_present_acpi() {
> ...
> 175     /// Checks if the kernel command line contains the "i8042.exist" option.
> 176     fn is_present_cmdline() -> bool {
> 177         I8042_EXIST.get().copied().unwrap_or(false)
> 178     }
> ```

Incorrect override handling (major): `is_present_cmdline()` collapses an absent command-line override and an explicit `i8042.exist=0` into the same `false` value, and `I8042Controller::new()` only consults it when ACPI says the controller is absent. On a machine where ACPI reports i8042 present, `i8042.exist=0` is parsed but ignored, so the driver still probes instead of honoring the skip request.

**Fix.** Shared with the documentation comment for `i8042.exist`: decide whether false values should be supported. If yes, keep the override tri-state, for example return `Option<bool>` from the command-line helper and match it before falling back to ACPI: `Some(false)` should return `I8042ControllerError::NotPresent`, `Some(true)` should force probing, and `None` should use `is_present_acpi()`. If no, reject or ignore false values consistently and document the parameter as force-present only.

### `kernel/comps/logger/src/console.rs` line 29

> ```diff
> 21     let devices = aster_console::all_devices_lock();
> ...
> 27         fn write_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> fmt::Result {
> 28             if self.0.is_empty() {
> 29                 ostd::early_print!("{}", s);
> 30             } else {
> ```

`no-io-under-spinlock` (major): `_print()` holds the `all_devices_lock()` `SpinLockGuard` when `write_str()` calls `ostd::early_print!`. With no registered consoles, every log write does serial output while local IRQs are disabled and the console-device spinlock is held, so a slow or blocking serial path can stall code that needs IRQ progress or the same lock.

**Fix.** Handle the empty-console case before constructing `Printer`, then drop `devices` before calling `ostd::early_print!`. For example, check `devices.is_empty()`, call `drop(devices)`, print with `ostd::early_print!("{}", args)`, and return.

## Documentation

### `book/src/kernel/linux-compatibility/kernel-parameters.md` line 23

> ```diff
> ### `console`
> 
> Select console devices for kernel messages.
> This parameter may be specified multiple times.
> Kernel messages are delivered to each listed console.
> 
> Examples:
> ```text
> console=ttyS0
> console=ttyS0 console=hvc0
> ```
> ```

`linux-compat-docs` (major): `console=ttyS0 console=hvc0` is documented as selecting multiple consoles, but `SystemConsole` still reads only `CONSOLES.first()`, so only the first listed console is used. A user following this example will expect messages on both `ttyS0` and `hvc0`, which the current code does not provide.

**Fix.** Either update the implementation to register every value from `CONSOLES`, or document the current behavior here, e.g. that `console` may appear multiple times but only the first supported value is currently honored.

### `book/src/kernel/linux-compatibility/kernel-parameters.md` line 62

> ```diff
> ### `i8042.exist`
> 
> Override ACPI's indication of whether a PS/2 (i8042) controller exists.
> 
> Valid values:
> - `1`, `on`, `yes`, `true` or no value — treat the i8042 controller as present (force probing)
> - `0`, `off`, `no`, `false` - treat the i8042 controller as absent (skip probing)
> ```

`linux-compat-docs` (major): `i8042.exist=0` is documented as forcing the controller absent, but the code only consults `i8042.exist` when ACPI already reports the controller absent. If ACPI reports it present, `i8042.exist=0` does not skip probing, so this compatibility entry advertises behavior users cannot rely on.

**Fix.** Shared with the correctness comment for `i8042.exist`: either implement false values as a real force-absent override, or document this as a force-present-only override where bare/true values force probing when ACPI says absent and false values are not a supported skip-probing control.

# Summary

The series adds a useful registry-based command-line parameter framework, moves `init`, `console`, and `i8042.exist` onto it, and adds reusable parsers plus boot-test coverage. The main risks are behavioral: unknown init arguments lose ordering and duplicates, Linux grouped CPU-list syntax is parsed incorrectly, and the `i8042.exist=0` path is documented and parsed but not honored when ACPI reports the controller present.

Top issues to fix first:

- Preserve command-line order for unknown parameters forwarded to `init`; the new `BTreeMap` grouping changes observable argv/envp behavior.
- Correct the `CpuList` grouped-range semantics to match Linux's `<used size>/<group size>` syntax.
- Decide the intended `i8042.exist` contract and make implementation and docs agree, preferably with tri-state override handling.
- Avoid serial I/O while holding the console-device spinlock in the early fallback logger.

Structurally, tighten the new public API before it grows users: avoid module-wide lint suppression, keep registry/value internals private behind constructors and getters, and put the new `inventory` dependency under workspace dependency management.

## Maintainability

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/Cargo.toml` line 13

> ```diff
>  component.workspace = true
>  log.workspace = true
>  ostd.workspace = true
>  spin.workspace = true
> +inventory = { git = "https://github.com/asterinas/inventory", rev = "9dce587" }
> ```

`workspace-deps` (minor): `kernel/comps/cmdline/Cargo.toml` adds `inventory` with an inline git specification while this workspace centralizes member dependencies in root `Cargo.toml` and member crates use `.workspace = true`. This creates another version pin to update independently.

**Fix.** Move the `inventory` specification to root `[workspace.dependencies]`, then depend on it here as `inventory.workspace = true`.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/lib.rs` line 179

> ```diff
> +    pub fn argv(&self) -> &Vec<CString> {
> +        &self.argv
> +    }
> +
> +    /// Gets the environment vector (`envp`) of the init process.
> +    pub fn envp(&self) -> &Vec<CString> {
> ```

`information-hiding` (minor): `InitprocArgs::argv` and `InitprocArgs::envp` return `&Vec<CString>`, which exposes the storage choice even though callers only need a borrowed sequence. That makes future representation changes harder and is less idiomatic than returning a slice.

**Fix.** Return slices from both getters: `pub fn argv(&self) -> &[CString]` and `pub fn envp(&self) -> &[CString]`. Existing callers can still use `.to_vec()`.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/lib.rs` line 284

> ```diff
> +pub struct KernelParam {
> +    pub name: &'static str,
> +    pub setup: fn(occurrences: &[(&str, Option<&str>)]),
> +    pub early: bool,
> +}
> ```

`getter-encapsulation` (major): `KernelParam` exposes `name`, `setup`, and `early` as public fields, even though they are registry internals used by the exported macros. External code can now construct and depend on the raw `KernelParam` representation, so changing registration details later becomes a public API break.

**Fix.** Make `KernelParam` fields private, add public constructor functions used by the macros, and mark any macro-only support surface as `#[doc(hidden)]`.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/types.rs` line 8

> ```diff
> +#![allow(dead_code)]
> +
> +extern crate alloc;
> ```

`narrow-lint-suppression` (major): `#![allow(dead_code)]` suppresses `dead_code` for the entire new `types` module, so any future unused helper added here will be silently accepted. The workspace uses `#[expect(dead_code)]` for intentional dead code, and the guideline asks suppressions to cover the smallest necessary scope.

**Fix.** Remove the module-level `#![allow(dead_code)]`. Either wire `CpuList` and `MetricU64` into real parameter users now, or mark only the currently unused items with narrow `#[expect(dead_code)]` plus the concrete planned use.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/types.rs` line 24

## Documentation

### `book/src/kernel/linux-compatibility/kernel-parameters.md` line 23

> ```diff
> ### `console`
> 
> Select console devices for kernel messages.
> This parameter may be specified multiple times.
> Kernel messages are delivered to each listed console.
> 
> Examples:
> ```text
> console=ttyS0
> console=ttyS0 console=hvc0
> ```
> ```

`linux-compat-docs` (major): `console=ttyS0 console=hvc0` is documented as selecting multiple consoles, but `SystemConsole` still reads only `CONSOLES.first()`, so only the first listed console is used. A user following this example will expect messages on both `ttyS0` and `hvc0`, which the current code does not provide.

**Fix.** Either update the implementation to register every value from `CONSOLES`, or document the current behavior here, e.g. that `console` may appear multiple times but only the first supported value is currently honored.

### `book/src/kernel/linux-compatibility/kernel-parameters.md` line 62

> ```diff
> ### `i8042.exist`
> 
> Override ACPI's indication of whether a PS/2 (i8042) controller exists.
> 
> Valid values:
> - `1`, `on`, `yes`, `true` or no value — treat the i8042 controller as present (force probing)
> - `0`, `off`, `no`, `false` - treat the i8042 controller as absent (skip probing)
> ```

`linux-compat-docs` (major): `i8042.exist=0` is documented as forcing the controller absent, but the code only consults `i8042.exist` when ACPI already reports the controller absent. If ACPI reports it present, `i8042.exist=0` does not skip probing, so this compatibility entry advertises behavior users cannot rely on.

**Fix.** Shared with the correctness comment for `i8042.exist`: either implement false values as a real force-absent override, or document this as a force-present-only override where bare/true values force probing when ACPI says absent and false values are not a supported skip-probing control.

 Incorrect override handling (major): `is_present_cmdline()` collapses an absent command-line override and an explicit `i8042.exist=0` into the same `false` value, and `I8042Controller::new()` only consults it when ACPI says the controller is absent. On a machine where ACPI reports i8042 present, `i8042.exist=0` is parsed but ignored, so the driver still probes instead of honoring the skip request.
 
-**Fix.** Keep the override tri-state, for example return `Option<bool>` from the command-line helper and match it before falling back to ACPI: `Some(false)` should return `I8042ControllerError::NotPresent`, `Some(true)` should force probing, and `None` should use `is_present_acpi()`.

If no, reject or ignore false values consistently and document the parameter as force-present only.

# Summary

The series adds a useful registry-based command-line parameter framework, moves `init`, `console`, and `i8042.exist` onto it, and adds reusable parsers plus boot-test coverage. The main risks are behavioral: unknown init arguments lose ordering and duplicates, Linux grouped CPU-list syntax is parsed incorrectly, and the `i8042.exist=0` path is documented and parsed but not honored when ACPI reports the controller present.

Top issues to fix first:

- Preserve command-line order for unknown parameters forwarded to `init`; the new `BTreeMap` grouping changes observable argv/envp behavior.
- Correct the `CpuList` grouped-range semantics to match Linux's `<used size>/<group size>` syntax.
- Decide the intended `i8042.exist` contract and make implementation and docs agree, preferably with tri-state override handling.
- Avoid serial I/O while holding the console-device spinlock in the early fallback logger.

Structurally, tighten the new public API before it grows users: avoid module-wide lint suppression, keep registry/value internals private behind constructors and getters, and put the new `inventory` dependency under workspace dependency management.

## Maintainability

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/Cargo.toml` line 13

> ```diff

`workspace-deps` (minor): `kernel/comps/cmdline/Cargo.toml` adds `inventory` with an inline git specification while this workspace centralizes member dependencies in root `Cargo.toml` and member crates use `.workspace = true`. This creates another version pin to update independently.

**Fix.** Move the `inventory` specification to root `[workspace.dependencies]`, then depend on it here as `inventory.workspace = true`.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/lib.rs` line 179

> ```diff

> +    }

`information-hiding` (minor): `InitprocArgs::argv` and `InitprocArgs::envp` return `{prompt}Vec<CString>`, which exposes the storage choice even though callers only need a borrowed sequence. That makes future representation changes harder and is less idiomatic than returning a slice.

**Fix.** Return slices from both getters: `pub fn argv({prompt}self) -> {prompt}[CString]` and `pub fn envp({prompt}self) -> {prompt}[CString]`. Existing callers can still use `.to_vec()`.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/lib.rs` line 284

> ```diff

`getter-encapsulation` (major): `KernelParam` exposes `name`, `setup`, and `early` as public fields, even though they are registry internals used by the exported macros. External code can now construct and depend on the raw `KernelParam` representation, so changing registration details later becomes a public API break.

**Fix.** Make `KernelParam` fields private, add public constructor functions used by the macros, and mark any macro-only support surface as `#[doc(hidden)]`.

## Correctness

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/lib.rs` line 412

> ```diff
> 380     // Step 1: Tokenize and group by normalized parameter name.
> 381     let mut grouped: BTreeMap<String, Vec<({prompt}str, Option<{prompt}str>)>> = BTreeMap::new();
> ...
> 412     for (name, occurrences) in {prompt}grouped {
> ...
> 421             } else if let Some((key, Some(value))) = occurrences.last().copied() {
> ...
> 426             } else if let Some((key, None)) = occurrences.last().copied() {
> ```

Incorrect argument forwarding (major): `dispatch_params()` stores pre-`--` arguments in a `BTreeMap` and later forwards unknown entries by iterating that map, so init arguments are sorted by key and duplicate bare arguments are collapsed with `occurrences.last()`. A command line such as `init=/usr/bin/busybox zarg aarg zarg` should pass `zarg`, `aarg`, `zarg` to `init` in that order, but this loop forwards only `aarg`, `zarg`.

**Fix.** Preserve forwarding order while still grouping recognized parameters. One practical shape is to build `registry` first, parse tokens in command-line order, push unknown `argv`/`envp` entries immediately, and only group occurrences for keys found in `registry`.

### `kernel/comps/cmdline/src/types.rs` line 166

> ```diff
> 110             // Grouped selection:
> 111             // for each group window [start+gb, start+gb+g), emit start+gb+within for within=0,stride,2*stride...
> ...
> 161     let offset = cpu - s.start;
> 162     if let Some(g) = s.group {
> ...
> 166         let in_group_offset = offset % g;
> 167         in_group_offset.is_multiple_of(s.stride)
> ```

Wrong CPU list parsing (major): `CpuList` treats the `:2/4` Linux CPU-list form as a stride of `2` inside each group of `4`, but Linux-style grouped CPU lists use the first number as the used-size of each group. For `CpuList::parse_param("0-9:2/4")`, `contains(1)` returns `false` and `contains(2)` returns `true`; the expected selected CPUs are `0`, `1`, `4`, `5`, `8`, and `9`.

**Fix.** Model the grouped form as `used_size/group_size` instead of `stride/group`. `contains()` should check `in_group_offset < used_size`, and `expand_bounded()` should emit the first `used_size` CPUs from each `group_size` window, clipping at `end`.

### `kernel/comps/i8042/src/controller.rs` line 177

> ```diff
> 132         if !Self::is_present_acpi() {
> ...
> 175     /// Checks if the kernel command line contains the "i8042.exist" option.
> 176     fn is_present_cmdline() -> bool {
> 177         I8042_EXIST.get().copied().unwrap_or(false)
> 178     }
> ```

Incorrect override handling (major): `is_present_cmdline()` collapses an absent command-line override and an explicit `i8042.exist=0` into the same `false` value, and `I8042Controller::new()` only consults it when ACPI says the controller is absent. On a machine where ACPI reports i8042 present, `i8042.exist=0` is parsed but ignored, so the driver still probes instead of honoring the skip request.

**Fix.** Shared with the documentation comment for `i8042.exist`: decide whether false values should be supported. If yes, keep the override tri-state, for example return `Option<bool>` from the command-line helper and match it before falling back to ACPI: `Some(false)` should return `I8042ControllerError::NotPresent`, `Some(true)` should force probing, and `None` should use `is_present_acpi()`. If no, reject or ignore false values consistently and document the parameter as force-present only.

### `kernel/comps/logger/src/console.rs` line 29

> ```diff
> 21     let devices = aster_console::all_devices_lock();
> ...
> 27         fn write_str({prompt}mut self, s: {prompt}str) -> fmt::Result {
> 28             if self.0.is_empty() {
> 29                 ostd::early_print!("{}", s);
> 30             } else {
> ```

`no-io-under-spinlock` (major): `_print()` holds the `all_devices_lock()` `SpinLockGuard` when `write_str()` calls `ostd::early_print!`. With no registered consoles, every log write does serial output while local IRQs are disabled and the console-device spinlock is held, so a slow or blocking serial path can stall code that needs IRQ progress or the same lock.

**Fix.** Handle the empty-console case before constructing `Printer`, then drop `devices` before calling `ostd::early_print!`. For example, check `devices.is_empty()`, call `drop(devices)`, print with `ostd::early_print!("{}", args)`, and return.

## Documentation

### `book/src/kernel/linux-compatibility/kernel-parameters.md` line 23

> ```diff
> ### `console`
> 
> Select console devices for kernel messages.
> This parameter may be specified multiple times.
> Kernel messages are delivered to each listed console.
> 
> Examples:
> ```text
> console=ttyS0
> console=ttyS0 console=hvc0
> ```
> ```

`linux-compat-docs` (major): `console=ttyS0 console=hvc0` is documented as selecting multiple consoles, but `SystemConsole` still reads only `CONSOLES.first()`, so only the first listed console is used. A user following this example will expect messages on both `ttyS0` and `hvc0`, which the current code does not provide.

**Fix.** Either update the implementation to register every value from `CONSOLES`, or document the current behavior here, e.g. that `console` may appear multiple times but only the first supported value is currently honored.

### `book/src/kernel/linux-compatibility/kernel-parameters.md` line 62
